searchText: Quick question about 7069 When does it return status code 2? Only when the upper 12 bits of the address is non-zero? When the contract being called does a REVERT or INVALID or runs out of gas. ASE violations cause the current frame to halt with an exceptional halt, like OOG. So to the calling frame it looks like a 2. Basically 1 corresponds to an error in the operation setting up the call (gas issues, not enough value, call stack too deep, etc), whereas 2 means the call was set up fine it's the contract that was called that had deliberate or accidental failures. Ah I see Wait, isn't 2 returned when setting up the call failed? I'm looking at the EIP here https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7069
